articles.description:
Hello 👋
TinyHumans and for a while now our whole team has been deep in AI tooling. The one thing that kept bugging us more than anything else was memory. Not the flashy stuff. Not the models, not the inference speed, not the prompting tricks. Just... memory. The boring, unglamorous, completely-broken part of almost every AI app we touched.
Here's the thing that was driving us crazy:
Vector similarity search retrieves what's similar. Not what's important. Not what's current. Just... similar.
Turns out the brain solved this millions of years ago...
Hermann Ebbinghaus figured it out in 1885. Memory retention drops roughly 50% within an hour unless it's reinforced. He called it the Forgetting Curve and it's not a flaw in human cognition. It's a feature. It's how the brain stays fast, lean, an…

articles.author: Jamie
articles.description:
Last month I kept asking the same question: why am I "busy" all day but shipping so little?
Two things were happening at once:
my AI coding costs kept jumping week to week
my attention kept getting nuked by feeds between coding blocks
I treated them as two separate problems for way too long.
feedback loops.
When you can't see cost in real time, you overspend.
Here are the 7 fixes that actually worked for me.
I now keep token/cost visibility in front of me during sessions.
That one change killed the "one more retry" spiral.
I used to default to expensive models for everything.
heavy reasoning: premium model
boilerplate/refactors/docs: cheaper model
Most work does not need top-tier reasoning.
Before hitting enter, I ask:
what exact output do I need?
what files are actually relevant?
what's the smallest acceptable pass?
This alone reduced wasteful reruns a lot.
Deleting apps never lasted.
I can still use DMs, search, and direct messages without infinite scroll.
Open-ended AI sessions are where costs explode.
I track:
biggest expensive session
why it blew up
one rule to prevent repeat
Tiny review, big compounding gains.
No feeds, no notifications, one coding objective.
TokenBar ($5): menu bar visibility for token/cost usage while coding → https://tokenbar.site


Monk Mode ($15): feed-level blocking on Mac so work blocks stay clean → https://mac.monk-mode.lifestyle



Both came from solving my own workflow mess as a solo builder.
If your AI bill feels random and your focus feels fragmented, try treating them as one system problem for a week.
You'll probably ship more and spend less.
articles.title: I stopped treating AI spend and doomscrolling as separate problems — 7 fixes that shipped real work
